To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the greedy face routing protocol with face ID support, GFRIS, achieves lower path stretch factors than GFG, GPS and GFG2 in most cases and even better than GOAFR+ when the network density is high.
GFRIS is an effective face routing protocol that can be deployed on any wireless network topology.

(i) GFRIS achieves the lowest path stretch factor among all face routing protocols in all node densities; (ii) GFRIS outperforms GOAFR+ by 5% on average in the worst case path stretch factor; (iii) GFRIS is the only face routing protocol that can guarantee packet delivery in all node densities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a face routing protocol that can achieve both guaranteed delivery and efficient routing.
the design and analysis of a new greedy routing protocol for mobile wireless networks that is capable of handling the face switch problem and provides efficient routing paths in the worst case.
the design of a new face routing protocol that has both guaranteed delivery and bounded path stretch.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GFRIS is the most efficient and reliable geographic face routing protocol for wireless networks.
GFRIS achieves the best performance among all face routing protocols in this study.
GFRIS is the first greedy face routing method that has the best worst case performance in terms of path stretch factor in all node densities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by actively probing each edge of the routing path for face ID, GFRIS can provide guaranteed face switch with a much lower path stretch factor than GFG2 and GFRIS can also provide bounded face traversal with a much lower overhead than GOAFR+ and GFR+.
, GFRIS has the lowest path stretch factor among all face routing protocols, while maintaining a guaranteed packet delivery ratio of 100%.
, GFRIS provides a better trade-off between path stretch factor and worst case performance in wireless networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
face ID is a very effective and simple tool in improving the worst case performance of greedy face routing.
face size is a key metric for face routing performance and should be used to trigger the face traversal direction switch.
face size is an important factor to determine the traversal direction of a face and face ID is an effective tool for face switching in wireless networks.
